## Pareto Distribution: PDF, CDF, and 80/20 Illustration

This document illustrates the Pareto distribution using simulation, along with plots of the PDF and CDF.  
We consider the standard Pareto distribution parameterized by a minimum value \( x_m \) and shape parameter \( \alpha \).

### Pareto PDF

\[
f(x) = \frac{\alpha x_m^\alpha}{x^{\alpha+1}}, \quad x \ge x_m
\]

### Pareto CDF

\[
F(x) = 1 - \left( \frac{x_m}{x} \right)^\alpha, \quad x \ge x_m
\]

The Pareto distribution is known for describing heavy-tailed phenomena and is frequently connected to the **80/20 rule**—the idea that a large proportion of outcomes is produced by a small portion of the population.

---

## R Code: Simulating, Visualizing, and Illustrating the Pareto Distribution

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# ----------------------------------------
# Parameters
# ----------------------------------------
xm <- 1        # minimum value
alpha <- 2.5   # shape parameter
n <- 5000      # sample size

# ----------------------------------------
# Pareto PDF and CDF functions
# ----------------------------------------
dpareto <- function(x, xm, alpha) {
  ifelse(x >= xm, (alpha * xm^alpha) / (x^(alpha + 1)), 0)
}

ppareto <- function(x, xm, alpha) {
  ifelse(x >= xm, 1 - (xm / x)^alpha, 0)
}

# ----------------------------------------
# Simulate Pareto data
# Inverse transform sampling:
# X = xm / (1 - U)^(1/alpha)
# ----------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
u <- runif(n)
x <- xm / (u)^(1 / alpha)
df <- data.frame(x = x)

# ----------------------------------------
# PDF curve
# ----------------------------------------
x_vals <- seq(xm, quantile(x, 0.99), length.out = 400)
pdf_vals <- dpareto(x_vals, xm, alpha)
cdf_vals <- ppareto(x_vals, xm, alpha)

pdf_df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, pdf = pdf_vals)
cdf_df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, cdf = cdf_vals)

# ----------------------------------------
# Plot PDF
# ----------------------------------------
p_pdf <- ggplot(pdf_df, aes(x, pdf)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.1, color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Pareto Distribution PDF",
       x = "x",
       y = "f(x)") +
  theme_minimal()

# ----------------------------------------
# Plot CDF
# ----------------------------------------
p_cdf <- ggplot(cdf_df, aes(x, cdf)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.1, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Pareto Distribution CDF",
       x = "x",
       y = "F(x)") +
  theme_minimal()

# ----------------------------------------
# 80/20 Principle Approximation
# Determine the value x* such that the top 20% of values hold most weight
# ----------------------------------------
threshold_80 <- quantile(df$x, 0.80)

# ----------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------
p_pdf
p_cdf

cat("Threshold for top 20% largest values (80/20 rule illustration):", threshold_80, "\n")

```
